evidence.notes: Founder-directed full catalog price refresh against official provider pricing pages (developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, docs.x.ai/docs/models, api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing, docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing, help.aliyun.com/zh/model-studio/model-pricing, platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat-k3, docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/pricing, console.groq.com/docs/model, openrouter.ai/api/v1/models), retrieved 2026-09-03. Four corrections: (1) gpt-5.6-sol's costOverride and its >272,000-token inputTokenPricingTiers entry were both roughly 20-25% above OpenAI's current published rate; corrected to $4/$20 (cache read $0.40, cache write $5) under 272K and $8/$30 (cache read $0.80, cache write $10) above it. gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-luna were re-verified and already matched exactly; the founder's initial flag named gpt-5.6-luna, but luna was correct and sol was the stale one. (2) gemini-3.1-pro-preview was missing Google's published pricing tier above 200,000 input tokens ($4.00 input, $18.00 output, $0.40 cache read); added as inputTokenPricingTiers. The base rate (2/12/0.2) already matched. (3) grok-4.5 was missing xAI's published pricing tier at or above 200,000 prompt tokens ($4.00 input, $12.00 output); added as inputTokenPricingTiers with no cache-read field since capabilitiesOverride.caching is false for this model. The base rate (2/6) already matched; xAI confirms the 500,000-token context window directly, so the bestFor label 'Long Context (1M)' is inaccurate copy, not a pricing fact, and is left for whoever owns that copy. (4) claude-sonnet-5: Decision #22 (docs/decisions/README.md) pinned this model's costOverride to $3/$15 on every date specifically because a provider introductory discount is a provider-cost fact, not a product price, and Anthropic's promotional $2/$10 window was scheduled to revert to $3/$15 on 2026-09-01. Anthropic's pricing page now states $2/$10 'is now the standard price' and that the scheduled increase 'will not occur', so the premise behind Decision #22 no longer holds. Per explicit founder instruction 2026-09-03, Decision #22 is retired (docs/decisions/README.md updated in the same change) and claude-sonnet-5.costOverride is set to the founder-selected standard tracking Anthropic's now-permanent rate: $2 input, $10 output, $0.20 cache read, $2.50 five-minute cache write, $4.00 one-hour cache write. packages/ai/model-registry/tests/catalog-policy.test.mjs was updated in the same change to assert the new values and cite the retirement instead of the reaffirmation. Every other model and OpenRouter route in the catalog was checked against its official source in this pass and found correct; minimax-m3's suspected missing cache-read price and >512K tier could not be confirmed against a first-party page (MiniMax's pricing pages are JS-rendered SPAs that returned no text to a direct fetch) and were left unchanged rather than applied from aggregator corroboration alone. Perplexity's per-request search fee and sonar-deep-research's citation/reasoning-token and search-query fees are confirmed to exist on Perplexity's pricing page but have no schema field to record them; flagged for a future schema change, not applied here.

Added GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash to the catalog and promoted the zhipu/glm family slot from glm-5.2 to glm-5.3 via the family-slots promotion script, then removed glm-5.2 from the roster and added it to retired-models.json. Official Z.ai documentation confirms glm-5.3 keeps GLM-5.2's shape (text-only input/output, 1,000,000-token context, function calling, structured output, streaming, context caching) but replaces the 5.2 thinking.type on/off toggle with mandatory reasoning at three effort levels (low, high, max via the reasoning_effort parameter; thinking.type now accepts only 'enabled'), and newly documents a 128,000-token output cap that 5.2 never published. GLM-5.3-Flash is a new addition, not a promotion target: it is the first natively multimodal GLM (text, image, video, PDF input; BUA/CUA computer-use and autonomous tool invocation) on the same 1,000,000-token context and 128,000-token output, same mandatory low/high/max reasoning. Pricing: glm-5.3 is unchanged from 5.2 at $1.40/M input, $4.40/M output, $0.26/M cache read; glm-5.3-flash is the current promotional rate of $0.075/M input, $0.25/M output, $0.015/M cache read, which Z.ai's pricing page lists as reverting to $0.15/$0.50/$0.03 on 2026-09-09 and must be re-verified before that date. Z.ai's pricing page was checked explicitly for day/night or peak/off-peak tiers on every model and carries none, so no time-of-day schedule applies (DeepSeek's peak-rate convention elsewhere in this catalog does not apply here). Benchmarks are omitted because Z.ai publishes none for either 5.3 model and carrying 5.2's numbers forward would be fabricated. GLM-5.3-Flash was left out of every provider default, task-routing slot, and tier list: those already resolve through family:zhipu/glm (unaffected by adding a non-family-pattern id), and Zhipu's provider block has no separate fast-tier route the way Google's flash-lite/flash split does, so inventing one was out of scope for this change. openrouter.ai/z-ai/glm-5.3 and openrouter.ai/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash confirm both slugs at matching context/output limits and pricing. Sources retrieved 2026-09-02: docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.3, docs.z.ai/guides/vlm/glm-5.3-flash, docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing, openrouter.ai/z-ai/glm-5.3, and openrouter.ai/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash.

Reverified current Qwen pricing against Alibaba Cloud Model Studio and tied catalog prices to the deployment scope the production adapter actually calls. The canonical Qwen adapter defaults to dashscope.aliyuncs.com, the Chinese-mainland deployment, not dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com. In that scope qwen3.5-flash uses three input-length bands: $0.029/$0.287 through 128K input, $0.115/$1.147 above 128K through 256K, and $0.172/$1.72 above 256K through 1M. qwen3.7-plus uses $0.276/$1.101 through 256K and $0.826/$3.301 above 256K through 1M; the former International-scope $0.40/$1.60 and $1.20/$4.80 values did not match the production endpoint and were removed. Implicit cache reads cost 20% of the active input band and explicit cache creation costs 125%, so every band carries its matching cache rates. Limited-time discounts remain excluded. Sources retrieved 2026-08-10: alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing and alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/context-cache. The pricing page identifies qwen3.5-flash as the current alias of the 2026-02-23 snapshot and qwen3.7-plus as the current alias of the 2026-05-26 snapshot.

Reverified the complete current OpenAI reasoning family against each official model page, the official GPT-5.6 model guidance, and the founder-provided official comparison screenshot. The published short-context rates were already correct: Sol $5 input / $0.50 cached input / $30 output, Terra $2 / $0.20 / $12, and Luna $0.20 / $0.02 / $1.20 per million tokens. All three publish a 1,050,000-token context window, 128,000 maximum output, and a 2026-02-16 knowledge cutoff. The cards do not publish a separate 922,000 maximum-input limit, so that previously derived field was removed rather than presented as an upstream fact. Requests above 272,000 input tokens are charged at 2x input and 1.5x output; the missing Terra and Luna long-context blocks are restored from those published multipliers, including the family's 1.25x cache-write rate. Image input supports low, high, original, and auto detail. Provider-hosted tools remain separate from AGI application capability flags: catalog search is true only because the Responses search harness is implemented, while computer use, code execution, and image generation stay false until their AGI execution paths are wired and verified. Sources retrieved 2026-08-10: developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol, developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra, developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna, and developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.

Corrected the stable internal runway-gen-4 catalog entry from the image-to-video-only gen4_turbo wire model to Runway's current text-to-video-capable gen4.5 model. Runway announced Gen-4.5 in December 2025; its POST /v1/text_to_video reference accepts gen4.5 but not gen4_turbo, constrains prompts to 1-1,000 UTF-16 code units, supports only 1280:720 landscape and 720:1280 portrait output, and accepts integer durations from 2-10 seconds. Runway prices gen4.5 at 12 credits per output second and sells credits for $0.01 each, so canonical cost is $0.12/second for the supported 720p orientations. The separate API changelog dates Gen-4.5 API availability to 2026-02-10; that API date is not the model release date. Removed the prior invented 4,000-token context because Runway documents a character limit, not a token context window. Documentation availability is not account provisioning: the entry remains availability=unavailable and Runway has no provider default until a live AGI-owned account probe returns 200. Runway also requires successful task output URLs to be downloaded and stored because they expire after 24-48 hours and must not be exposed directly. Sources retrieved 2026-08-09: docs.dev.runwayml.com/api, docs.dev.runwayml.com/assets/inputs, docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/models, docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/pricing, docs.dev.runwayml.com/api-details/api_changelog, and docs.dev.runwayml.com/assets/outputs.

Added GPT-5.6 family (sol/terra/luna) as availability:"coming_soon" (LIVE 404 on our key 2026-07-10, NOT provisioned); bare gpt-5.6 will alias to Sol at GA (no canonicalization alias added this wave, the family is non-routable while coming_soon); kept OUT of tierAllowedModels/SLOT_REGISTRY/taskRouting/defaultModel (enforced by new check:availability-invariant). 5.6 reasoning ladder none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max (max above xhigh). Ultra (multi_agent.enabled + max_concurrent_subagents, beta responses_multi_agent=v1), Pro (reasoning.mode:"pro"), persistent reasoning (reasoning.context), and programmatic tool calling (tool type programmatic_tool_calling + allowed_callers) are RESPONSES-API-ONLY and INERT this wave, our web chat route uses /chat/completions, so the at-GA wave must add a Responses path for those four; effort/vision/tools work on the existing chat path. Added inert tierPolicy.minTier authored data (NOT used to derive tierAllowedModels this wave, all budget models stay available for testing per founder). Gemini 3.x request path migrated to thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel (thinkingBudget kept as legacy fallback). The launch-era pricing figures in this historical note were superseded by the current official rates verified in the top 2026-08-10 entry; reasoningDots remains 5/4/3.

Voice/audio lineup swept live against developers.openai.com/api/docs/models and elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models. REMOVED tts-1 + tts-1-hd (November 2023, superseded); the previous wave kept them because gpt-4o-mini-tts pricing was not then verifiable, it now is. ADDED gpt-4o-mini-tts ($0.60/1M input text, $12/1M output audio, 2k input cap, default snapshot gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15), which also removes a unit inconsistency: tts-1 was priced per 1M CHARACTERS in inputCost, a field every other model uses for dollars per 1M TOKENS. FIXED gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe: both carried whisper-1 leftovers after that model was retired, released "September 2022" (whisper-1's date) and costOverride.inputCost 0.006 (whisper-1's $/minute), which published transcription at $0.006/1M tokens against real prices of $2.50/1M and $1.25/1M, understating by ~417x and ~208x. Now $2.50/$10 and $1.25/$5 with 16k context. Desktop TTS defaults fixed in the same pass: ElevenLabs eleven_monolingual_v1 was REMOVED upstream 2026-07-09 and was still the fallback for any user who never set a model, so unconfigured ElevenLabs playback was calling a nonexistent model, now eleven_flash_v2_5; OpenAI tts-1 -> gpt-4o-mini-tts. NOT DONE (follow-up): TTS has no routing slot, so apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/features/speech/tts.rs still hardcodes both defaults; a voice_tts slot would only cover OpenAI because the catalog carries no ElevenLabs provider. Also unaddressed: gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize (new upstream, not added), and managed-cloud transcription is rate-limited but never metered against the usage balance.

Founder flagged that gpt-4o-mini-tts carries a Deprecated badge on the developers.openai.com model catalog listing, correct, and it landed the same day we adopted it. Resolved against four sources: the listing badges it Deprecated; its own model page shows NO deprecation banner and no shutdown date; the deprecations table has no family-level row for it (only snapshot gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-03-20 -> -2025-12-15, shut down 2026-07-23); and the text-to-speech guide still calls it the newest and most reliable TTS model. Decisive fact: it is the ONLY model OpenAI serves on /v1/audio/speech, gpt-audio-1.5's model page lists "Speech generation | v1/audio/speech | Not supported". So there is no newer member of this family to move to. Marked deprecated:true (compile.mjs then sets selectable:false) and KEPT, because removing it would leave the OpenAI TTS path with no model at all. NOT ADDED, deliberately: the realtime family (gpt-realtime-2.1, gpt-realtime-2.1-mini, gpt-realtime-translate, gpt-realtime-whisper). Three reasons, ModelType has no "realtime" member, so it is a schema change across the TS union, the registry schema and both Rust registries; we ship no duplex audio path (founder-gated on a realtime provider plus echo cancellation); and registering them live would advertise capability we do not have. Recorded as VOICE-REALTIME-FAMILY-ABSENT so the ids do not need re-researching: gpt-realtime-2.1 ($4/$24 text, $32/$64 audio, $0.40 cached, 128k ctx, 32k max out) and gpt-realtime-2.1-mini ($0.60/$2.40 text, $10/$20 audio) are the current heads; gpt-realtime, gpt-realtime-mini, gpt-audio, gpt-audio-mini and every gpt-4o-audio/gpt-4o-realtime variant shut down 2027-01-20. gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe carry NO deprecated badge and stay as-is.

Added the two OpenRouter router routes the product had no entry for: openrouter/auto (Auto Router) and openrouter/free (Free Models Router), and set open_router.defaultModel to openrouter/auto, which was previously empty so the provider had no route at all. Every field is read from https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models retrieved 2026-08-29 with a live key. Auto Router: canonical_slug openrouter/auto, 2,000,000 context, tokenizer "Router", modality text+image+file+audio+video->text+image, and supported_parameters including reasoning, reasoning_effort, tools, tool_choice and structured_outputs, hence reasoning.control "effort". Free Models Router: canonical_slug openrouter/free, 200,000 context, modality text+image->text, pricing prompt "0" and completion "0", and supported_parameters including reasoning_effort, tools and structured_outputs. Both routes report pricing that is resolved per request, auto returns "-1" for prompt and completion because cost follows the model it selects, so no per-million rate is recorded here and reservation must price the resolved route, not the router. No benchmarks are recorded because OpenRouter publishes none for either router, and carrying a member model's numbers forward would be fabricated. openrouter/auto is recorded with inputCost/outputCost 0 because ModelMetadata requires both and the router publishes no rate of its own; managed metering must price the model the router actually resolved (the completion response reports it) rather than the router record, so this route is safe on BYOK, where OpenRouter bills the key holder directly, and must not be exposed on a metered managed plan until resolved-route pricing is wired. openrouter/free is genuinely zero-rated ("0"/"0" from the provider).

Both router routes were exercised end to end against the live API after the account key was rotated. openrouter/auto returned HTTP 200 in 752ms and reported routing to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, confirming the earlier note that the router itself publishes no rate and that metering must price the resolved model. openrouter/free returned HTTP 200 and routed to free members (nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free, minimax/minimax-m2.7:free) with usage.cost 0, confirming the zero rating. Both free members are reasoning models whose reasoning tokens count against max_tokens: a 16-token cap returned empty content while a 200-token cap returned the expected text with finish_reason "stop" and 31 reasoning tokens. The product default is DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 8192, so this is not reachable in normal use, but any caller that lowers the cap for a free-router turn must leave room for reasoning tokens.

Adjudicated three input-budget rows a litellm cross-check flagged, reading Google's own pages rather than either snapshot. gemini-3.1-pro-preview: the model card publishes an input token limit of 1,048,576 and an output token limit of 65,536, so the recorded 2,000,000 was wrong and the snapshot's 1,048,576 was right; corrected in models.synced.json, where models.dev already carried 1,048,576. Google markets this model at 1M scale and no 2,000,000 or 2,097,152 figure appears on the card or in its context-caching section. gemini-3.1-flash-image: the card publishes an input token limit of 131,072 and an output token limit of 32,768, so BOTH sides were wrong, the recorded 1,000,000 and litellm's 65,536. gemini-omni-flash-preview: no model card exists at that id (it 404s) and the models overview table lists only gemini-omni-1.1-flash; the pricing page carries the preview id as a billing SKU whose model-card link resolves to the shared Gemini Omni Flash card, which publishes a combined context window of 1,048,576 tokens. The recorded 4,000 was a video-model placeholder shared with the veo-3.1 rows and litellm's 131,072 matches nothing Google publishes. Prices on all three rows were re-read at the same time and are unchanged: gemini-3.1-pro-preview $2.00/$12.00 with $0.20 caching under 200k tokens and $4.00/$18.00/$0.40 above it; gemini-3.1-flash-image $0.50 input, $3.00 text output, $60.00 image output; gemini-omni-flash-preview $1.50 input, $9.00 text output, $17.50 video output. Sources retrieved 2026-09-01: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.1-pro-preview, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-3.1-flash-image, https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-omni-flash.

DeepSeek publishes a peak/off-peak rate card, and both V4 rows carried figures that match neither half of it. Peak is $0.44/$1.32 per 1M with a $0.014 cache hit for deepseek-v4-flash and $1.32/$3.96 with a $0.044 cache hit for deepseek-v4-pro; off-peak is exactly half of each, and peak hours are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC Monday through Friday. Both rows now carry the peak rate as a curation costOverride, because peak is the only figure never undercut on any date and the schema has no field for a time-of-day split; the same reasoning moved providers.deepseek.defaultPricing, the cost-calculator fallback for unrecognised deepseek ids, from $0.14/$0.28 to $0.44/$1.32. The prior values ($0.14/$0.28/$0.0028 for flash, $0.435/$0.87/$0.003625 for pro) came from models.dev, which still publishes them for the first-party deepseek provider; litellm's first-party deepseek entry independently agrees with the peak rate. The pro row additionally asserted that DeepSeek made a 75% launch discount permanent on 2026-05-22, no discount, promotion or expiry language appears anywhere on DeepSeek's pricing page, so that claim is withdrawn. The override lives in curation rather than the synced snapshot so a later models.dev refresh cannot silently restore the undercharge. gpt-image-2 was checked in the same pass and is correct as recorded: OpenAI publishes an image row at $8.00 input, $2.00 cached input, $30.00 output and a separate text row at $5.00 input, $1.25 cached input, and this entry carries the image row throughout, so the $2.00 cache read stands and the $1.25 a snapshot reports is the text row. Sources retrieved 2026-09-01: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing.
